target_customer: Operators of nanosatellites (10 to 12 kg) wanting dedicated, frequent launches to low Earth and sun-synchronous orbit
problem: Small satellites mostly rode as secondary payloads on large rockets. Bagaveev planned a small rocket with 3D-printed aerospike engines to launch nanosatellites on demand, with a stated goal of weekly launches.
business_model: launch services priced per nanosatellite (planned; no launches occurred)

founders.name: Nadir Bagaveyev
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no background. A search summary of an aggregator calls him a US Army veteran and propulsion engineer, which no opened source confirms, so it is not recorded.

technical_complexity.rationale: Developing a 3-ton orbital rocket with 3D-printed aerospike engines for both stages was research-grade propulsion engineering and needed large capital, from a one-founder team.

defensibility.rationale: Orbital launch needs scarce propulsion expertise and range access, which would be hard to copy if achieved, but no working engine or customer contract is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source reports any acquirer. Trackers list the company as wound down or dormant, with no launch ever reported.

market_need_then: The YC page frames demand as nanosatellite operators needing dedicated small launches. No dated customer, order or revenue evidence was found.

brand_strength.rationale: The name looks like the founder's surname (inferred, not sourced) and branding searches found nothing, only surname pages and unrelated trademarks. It was hard to spell, with the founder's own name spelled Bagaveyev.

outcome_analysis: Bagaveev was a one-founder Winter 2015 YC company designing a 3-ton small-satellite launcher with 3D-printed aerospike engines, backed by YC and Boost with reported seed funding of about $120K to $730K in total depending on the database. No funding after 2015 and no launch were found, and a niche tracker lists it as wound down around 2020. The cause is not public, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: No company website is listed on the YC page, and none was found, so there was no site to fetch. Funding conflict: CB Insights total about $730K over four rounds (only one round of $0.12M, March 2015, was itemised), Spacebandits $655K, newspace.im $0.67M; the gap between the itemised round and the totals is unresolved. The YC-dated seed rests on a single database. Boost backing comes only from the YC page text, with no amount or date. Gust gives founding November 2013 and San Mateo; the YC page says San Francisco. Wind-down around 2020 comes from a niche tracker (Spacebandits), and Newspace.im calls it dormant (updated August 2023). The dated competitor searches found only post-2018 articles, so the list is empty.
